title: lava check --json
description: The one-command verification: boot, wiring, routes, features, env, commands, the map, and the app's own suite, merged into one problem list and one exit code. `sections` says WHICH part of the app is broken before any individual problem is read; the envelope's `problems` is ordered to act on: fatals before warnings, and within each severity a runnable fix before one that needs judgement. It survives a failed boot on purpose — a red suite is often the reason an app cannot boot, so the tests still run and the report carries both. /2 added `map` to the section enum: a consumer switching exhaustively on the nine names of /1 would not have handled it, and the frozen-/N rule makes that a new version rather than an edit.

sections.description: Always all nine, in the order an app is built, so a consumer can index them rather than search. A clean run has every section ok or skipped.

status.description: skipped applies to `tests` when no suite ran, and to `env` and `map` under --quick, whose checks are sweeps --quick does not run. Under --strict a warn makes its section failed.

detail.description: The problem codes found, then the test summary when there was a run. Empty for a clean section.

counts.description: What boot found. All zero when the app did not boot — the counts come from the booted app, not from re-reading files. `map` has no count here: the section reports a verdict, not a quantity.

tests.description: The suite's results, or null when no run happened — see the tests section's detail for which of --quick, --no-tests, or a missing runner it was.

strict.description: Whether warnings were escalated to failures for this run.

quick.description: Whether this run skipped the suite and the sweeps (all-features, env, and the map).
